title: Risk Assessments & Method Statements
whatItIs: A risk assessment looks at the hazards in a job, who could be harmed and how, and the precautions needed. A method statement then sets out, step by step, how the job will be done safely.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST make a suitable and sufficient assessment of the risks to their employees and to others affected.
An employer with five or more employees MUST record the significant findings.
The assessment MUST be reviewed if it may no longer be valid or there's been a significant change.

keyFacts: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm.
Method statements aren't required by law, but they're an effective way to explain a safe system of work.

visual.caption: The five steps of a risk assessment (HSG150)

rows: The job, the place, equipment, materials, chemicals
Your team, other firms' workers, visitors, the public
Remove the hazard; if you can't, control the risk
Required with five or more employees
When the job or the way it's done changes

a.label: Risk assessment
points: Finds the hazards, who is at risk and the controls

b.label: Method statement
points: Sets out in order how the job is done safely

onTheTest.question: When deciding on precautions for a hazardous job, what should be considered first?
options: Can the hazard be removed completely?
How to word the risk assessment
Who is to blame if it goes wrong
onTheTest.why: HSG150: first ask whether the hazard can be removed, eg by doing the job another way or using a less hazardous material. Only if not do you control the risk.

onTheTest.question: Halfway through a job the work method changes significantly. What must happen to the risk assessment?
options: It must be reviewed and changed if needed
Nothing until the job is finished
It must be sent to HSE
It only needs a new date on it
onTheTest.why: Management Regulations, reg 3(3): an assessment must be reviewed if it may no longer be valid or there's been a significant change, and any changes needed must be made.

traps: Remove the hazard first; only if you can't do you move on to controlling it and protecting people.
Firms with fewer than five employees still assess risks; they just needn't record them.
A method statement is good practice, not a legal requirement. The risk assessment is the legal duty.
